question: What is the physical appearance of a smooth muscle cell under a microscope?

options.A: Spindle-shaped with a single central nucleus
options.B: Short and branched with intercalated discs
options.C: Long and cylindrical with multiple peripheral nuclei

explanation: Smooth muscle cells are tapered at both ends, forming a spindle shape, and contain one nucleus right in the middle. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T11#GNS121_U3_T11_h1)

question: Where is smooth muscle tissue primarily located in the human body?

options.D: Exclusively in the walls of the heart

explanation: Smooth muscle lines organs like the gut, blood vessels, and bladder to help move substances through the body. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T11#GNS121_U3_T11_h1)

question: What structures take the place of Z-lines in smooth muscle cells to anchor thin filaments?
explanation: Dense bodies serve as the anchoring points for thin filaments in smooth muscle, similar to Z-discs in skeletal muscle. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T11#GNS121_U3_T11_h2)

question: Why does a smooth muscle cell twist during contraction?

options.A: Intermediate filaments dissolve in the cytoplasm
options.B: Myosin fibers shorten from end to end
options.C: Calcium ions twist the cell membrane
options.D: Actin filaments pull on anchored dense bodies

explanation: The diagonal arrangement of contractile units pulling on dense bodies causes the cell to shorten and twist during activation. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T11#GNS121_U3_T11_h2)

question: Which regulatory protein binds calcium in smooth muscle instead of troponin?
explanation: Calmodulin acts as the primary calcium sensor that initiates the contraction cascade in smooth muscle cells. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T11#GNS121_U3_T11_h3)

question: What is the main job of myosin light chain kinase (MLCK) in smooth muscle?

options.A: Adding a phosphate group to myosin so it can bind actin
options.B: Breaking down ATP to help the muscle relax
options.C: Connecting adjacent cell membranes at gap junctions
options.D: Pumping calcium back into the storage sacs

explanation: Activated MLCK adds a phosphate group to myosin, changing its shape so it can interact with actin to cause contraction. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T11#GNS121_U3_T11_h3)

question: What specialized cell junctions allow single-unit smooth muscle to contract synchronously?
explanation: Gap junctions create low-resistance electrical pathways that let action potentials pass freely from one cell to the next. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T11#GNS121_U3_T11_h4)

question: Where is multi-unit smooth muscle most likely found in the body?
explanation: Multi-unit smooth muscle is found where precise, independent motor control is needed, such as the iris adjusting pupil size. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T11#GNS121_U3_T11_h4)

question: What are the swollen regions on nerve fibers that release neurotransmitters onto smooth muscle called?
explanation: Autonomic neurons form a series of bulbous swellings called varicosities that release neurotransmitters over a broad area of smooth muscle. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T11#GNS121_U3_T11_h5)

question: Which factor CANNOT directly stimulate smooth muscle contraction?
explanation: Somatic motor nerves supply skeletal muscle under voluntary control, whereas smooth muscle responds to autonomic, hormonal, and local stimuli. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T11#GNS121_U3_T11_h5)

question: What term describes the ability of smooth muscle to maintain tension over a wide range of resting lengths?
explanation: Plasticity allows hollow organs like the bladder to adapt to large volume changes without losing their ability to contract. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T11#GNS121_U3_T11_h6)

question: Why is the latch state helpful for smooth muscle in blood vessel walls?

options.A: It maintains blood vessel tone using very little energy
options.B: It speeds up the rate of nerve signal conduction
options.C: It prevents the vessel from ever relaxing under pressure
options.D: It allows the blood vessel to beat rhythmically like the heart

explanation: The latch state lets myosin and actin remain attached for prolonged periods without constantly burning ATP, which is ideal for continuous blood pressure regulation. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T11#GNS121_U3_T11_h6)

question: What happens in airway smooth muscle to directly trigger an asthma attack?

options.A: Permanent relaxation of the muscle fibers
options.B: Breakdown of dense bodies by cellular enzymes
options.C: Sudden spasm and excessive narrowing of the muscle
options.D: Loss of cell connections in the small airways

explanation: Asthma involves sudden, strong contractions of the smooth muscle lining the airways, which narrows airflow. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T11#GNS121_U3_T11_h7)

question: A patient has high blood pressure due to narrowed blood vessels. Which tissue layer in the vessels causes this constriction?

options.A: Skeletal muscle fibers in the arm

explanation: The middle layer (tunica media) of blood vessels is composed mainly of smooth muscle, which controls vessel diameter and resistance. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T11#GNS121_U3_T11_h7)
